objective: C03: rule out fixed-defect repairs by an exact bipartite-frame spectrum formula, and eliminate all 341 eligible labeled Petersen triangle expansions by an explicit divisible-cycle construction.

atomic_claims.text: Replacing one part of a cubic 3-connected bipartite frame by Petersen-minus-vertex bricks gives spectra consisting of t copies of 5 plus 5r for each quotient cycle of length 2r; each quotient factor has 2^t lifts.
For Hamiltonian frames with 3 dividing t, the minimum bad-cycle count is t=n/10 and the minimum bad-vertex count is 5t=n/2; prisms supply an unbounded family in the root order domain.
If S is nonempty, v lies in S, and G-v is Hamiltonian, triangle expansion at S has a spanning 2-factor (3,N-3), so the stronger condition holds whenever 3 divides N.
All 341 labeled Petersen expansions with expansion-set sizes 1,4,7,10 are non-Hamiltonian yet have the explicit divisible spectra (3,9), (3,15), (3,21), (3,27).
The bounded generator-side run checked all 341 explicit triangle factors and matched direct spectra with the transfer formula on the K3,3, cube-prism, and hexagonal-prism frames.

assumptions: All graphs are finite and simple; 3-connected means vertex connectivity at least three.
P3 means a selected two-edge path on three distinct vertices, not necessarily an induced subgraph.
risks: Candidate proofs and exact generator checks do not produce mathematical EvidenceLinks or Result admission.
C01 candidate lemmas are dependencies, not admitted mathematical Evidence.
The order-40 frame expansion is outside the root order domain and is used only to test the general transfer formula.
The 341 count concerns labeled expansion subsets, not isomorphism classes or all cubic graphs of those orders.
The spectral calculation alone is not asserted to yield a P3-factor for every inflated bipartite frame.
No minimum counterexample order or research novelty claim is made in this iteration.
